title: Pip and the Peep-Peep Mystery
moral: When we are curious and gentle, we discover wonderful new things.
description: Pip hears a teeny, tiny peep-peep and just HAS to find out who made it! With Tumble and Nana Hoot he meets ducklings, a lamb and a calf on a giggly Baby Animal Hunt. Learn the names of baby animals in this funny animated story about curiosity for kids aged 3 to 8.
intro: Hi friends! Welcome to Little Lantern Stories! Today's story is... Pip and the Peep-Peep Mystery! Can you guess who says peep?

popups.sub: every baby has a special name

narration.text: Guess what? One sunny morning, Pip the little fox heard a teeny, tiny sound. Peep... peep... peep!

narration.speaker: pip
narration.text: Who said peep? I just HAVE to find out!
Then... BOING! Tumble popped up from behind the bush!

narration.speaker: tumble
narration.text: Was it my tummy? Sometimes my tummy goes peep! HONK! Oopsie-trunk, no, that was my nose.

narration.speaker: nana
narration.text: Hoo-hoo-HOO! It's a baby animal! Every baby animal has its own special name. Let's go on a Baby Animal Hunt!

narration.text: First stop, Lily Pond! A mummy duck was swimming with three fluffy babies. Peep, peep, peep!

narration.speaker: pip
narration.text: I know! A baby duck is called a... duck-a-doodle-doo!
Hee-hee! No, Pip, that's a rooster song! A baby duck is called a DUCKLING. Can you say it? Duckling!
Pip leaned closer... and closer... and, wheee! He slid down the muddy bank. SPLOOSH!

narration.speaker: tumble
narration.text: Oopsie-trunk! Ducklings, was that your peep? Oh. They say it came from somewhere else.
Next, the friends skipped up Clover Hill to see a woolly mummy sheep and her little baby.
What do YOU think a baby sheep is called? Have a think!

narration.speaker: tumble
narration.text: Ooh, ooh! Is it... a cloud with legs?
Hee-hee! It's a LAMB! A baby sheep is a lamb. You're so smart!
Then the fluffy wool tickled Tumble's trunk. Ah... ah... AH-CHOOOO! Pip spun round like a wibble-wobble top!
Over at Sunny Farm, a big spotty cow said MOOOO! And next to her stood a wobbly-legged baby.
A baby cow is called a CALF. Can you say calf?

narration.speaker: tumble
narration.text: Hey! Nana says a baby elephant is called a calf too! I'm a calf!

narration.speaker: pip
narration.text: WHAT? You're a COW?!

narration.speaker: tumble
narration.text: No, silly! I'm an elephant calf! HONK HONK!
The peep-peep was close now! Pip zoomed ahead shouting, COME OUT, LITTLE PEEPER! And... the peeping stopped.

narration.speaker: nana
narration.text: Shh, Pip. Babies get shy when it's loud. Let's tiptoe, whisper, and look very closely.
So Pip tiptoed. CRUNCH! A crispy leaf. He tiptoed again. CRACK! A twiggy stick. Oops!
Then big Tumble tiptoed... and he didn't make one single sound! Not one!

narration.speaker: tumble
narration.text: Elephants have soft, squishy feet. Shhhh!
They peeked behind the berry bush. And there was a mummy hen, sitting next to a cosy nest!
Crack... crack... CRACK! Out popped fluffy yellow babies! A baby hen is called a CHICK.
How many chicks can YOU count? Count with your finger!
Five chicks! One, two, three, four, five! The last one was still in its egg!

narration.speaker: pip
narration.text: We found the peep-peep! Super-duper... I mean, super-duper QUIETLY!
The sun got hot, so Tumble made shade with his big flappy ears. And Pip gently brought seeds and a little cup of water.
Mummy Hen clucked a happy thank-you. Cluck-cluck! The chicks snuggled up, warm and safe.

narration.speaker: nana
narration.text: When I was little, I was an OWLET. A baby owl is an owlet. Zzzzz...
Uh-oh! Nana fell asleep, and her glasses slid down her beak... wheee... BONK!

narration.speaker: nana
narration.text: Hoo! I'm awake! I'm awake! And a baby fox, like Pip, is called a KIT!
Let's remember! What is a baby duck called?
A DUCKLING! Peep, peep! Hooray!
And what is a baby sheep called?
A LAMB! Wow, you remembered everything!

narration.speaker: tumble
narration.text: And don't forget me! I'm a calf! HONK!

narration.text: That night, Mummy Hen brought her chicks to Nana's oak. Goodnight, ducklings! Goodnight, lamb! Goodnight, calf!

narration.speaker: pip
narration.text: Asking questions and looking closely is the best! What will we find tomorrow?

narration.speaker: tumble
narration.text: Maybe a baby elephant who doesn't sneeze! Ah... ah... AH-CHOO! Hee-hee. Nope!
And Nana Hoot? She was already snoring. Peep, peep... goodnight!
